idea-plugin.name: Livy Query Console
idea-plugin.description:
Livy Query Console lets you run Spark, PySpark, and Spark SQL code on a remote cluster via Apache Livy directly from your JetBrains IDE.

It is designed for quick exploration, debugging, and day-to-day data engineering workflows: write a snippet, run it in a Livy interactive session, inspect the output, and iterate — without leaving the IDE.

Key features

  • Livy work file: open a dedicated reusable Livy work surface, route editor selection/current line/whole file into it, and execute snippets without leaving the IDE workflow. The work file follows the bound execution kind (`sql`, `pyspark` / `python`, or fallback plain Spark text) and reuses host-IDE highlighting where available.
  • Result viewer: each run is added as a new tab with:
    • Raw response (full JSON output from Livy)
    • Pretty view (human-readable summary including errors and stack traces)
    • Table view for Spark ASCII tables (e.g. output of df.show())
  • Session logs: view Livy session logs in a separate dialog to diagnose cluster/session issues.
  • Statements browser: list recent statements in a session and inspect their state and output status.
  • Tool Window: a “Livy Sessions” tool window that shows active sessions and provides quick actions (refresh, logs, statements).
  • Connection profiles: keep multiple named Livy targets with per-profile session kind, resource parameters, and session management strategy.
  • Local history: recent snippets and the last draft per profile can be restored locally for quick rerun/reuse. This is plain-text local persistence, not notebook or remote session restore.

Typical usage

  1. Open Livy: Open Work File (Tools → Livy) or use the Livy editor/project popup actions.
  2. Choose the connection profile to bind the work file or run action to.
  3. Route a selection/current line/whole file into Livy, or use Run Current / Run File inside the work file.
  4. Inspect results, logs, and statements, then iterate.

Note: This plugin requires access to a running Apache Livy server. Authentication/SSL behavior depends on your environment (for corporate/self-signed certificates you may need to add the CA certificate to the JetBrains Runtime trust store).

Current scope: the plugin supports multiple named connection profiles for direct Livy HTTP(S) connectivity. Existing work files and loaded session views stay bound to the profile snapshot they were opened with. Optional local history stores recent snippets and the last draft per profile in plain text on the local machine only. SQL work files support a narrow semicolon-delimited current-statement heuristic; PySpark/plain Spark work files stay on selection-or-file execution semantics. This is a lightweight execution workflow, not notebook persistence or semantic Spark language tooling. Advanced auth flows such as auth headers/tokens, cookies, Kerberos, OAuth, and secure credential storage are not implemented yet.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
What's new in 1.5

  • Profile-safe execution: consoles, work files, and loaded session views stay bound to the captured Livy profile snapshot instead of silently drifting when settings change.
  • Reusable Livy work file: editor/project popup actions can open source in a dedicated Livy work file, rerun recent snippets from local history, restore the last draft per profile/kind, and navigate back to source.
  • Language-aware editor surface: the work file now reflects the bound execution kind, reuses host-IDE SQL/Python highlighting when available, and supports a narrow SQL current-statement run heuristic.
  • Sessions workflow improvements: the Livy Sessions tool window now supports safe termination of plugin-managed sessions plus panel-level auto-refresh with a configurable interval.
  • Better reliability: the work-file/editor run path was tightened to avoid wrong-target drift, duplicate request application, and editor-provider lifecycle issues.
  • Honest product boundary: the plugin now says explicitly where support stops: direct Livy connectivity with profiles and local plain-text history, not advanced auth or notebook semantics.
